The breakup of the total number of employees of a company working in different offices (A to E), in degrees, is given in the pie chart. The total number of employees = 2400.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/60d1c052f70af48e92d9f5c5ed29c60ff69bc6ad745b8ad93bac5156087b89b8.png] 

If the percentage of male employees in office C is 20% and that of female employees in E is 40%, then what is the ratio of the numbers of female employees in E to that of female employees in C?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Male employees in office C = 20%

Female employees in office E = 40%

**To Find:**

Ratio of Female employees in E : Female employees in C

**Calculation:**

Total female employees in office C = 2400 × (54/360) × 80%

⇒ 360 × 80%

⇒ 288

Total female employees in office E = 2400 × (72/360) × 40%

⇒ 480 × 40%

⇒ 192

Ratio = 192 : 288

⇒ 2 : 3

**∴ Required answer is 2 : 3.**

questions.question: AB is the diameter of a circle with centre O. C and D are two points on the circle on either side of AB, such that ∠CAB = 52° and ∠ABD = 47°. What is the difference (in degrees) between the measures of ∠CAD and ∠CBD?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

∠CAB = 52° and ∠ABD = 47°

**Concept used:**

The angle subtended by the diameter at any point on the circumference is equal to 90°

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9fbfeea21bd1cb1f145ad930e85feae1d41e56c2c28d0c31d246ede66a506fcf.png] 

According to the concept,

∠ACB = ∠ADB = 90°

So, ∠CBA = 180° - (90° + 52°)

⇒ 180° - 142°

⇒ 38°

Similarly,

∠BAD = 180° - (90° + 47°)

⇒ 180° - 137°

⇒ 43°

So, ∠CAD = 52° + 43°

⇒ 95°

∠CBD = 38° + 47°

⇒ 85°

Now,

∠CAD - ∠CBD = 95° - 85°

⇒ 10°

**∴ The difference (in degrees) between the measures of ∠CAD and ∠CBD is 10.**

questions.question: Two trains are running on parallel tracks in the same direction at the speed of 80 km/h and 90 km/h, respectively. The trains crossed each other in 3 minutes. If the length of one train is 230 m, then what is the length (in m) of the other train?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of the two trains is 80 km/h and 90 km/h

They cross each other in 3 minutes

**Concept used:**

Time = Distance/speed

Relative speed = When two bodies moving in the same direction then their relative speed of them will be different of the individual speed

**Calculation:**

3 min = 180 sec

The relative speed of the trains = 90 - 80

⇒ 10 km/h

Speed in m/sec = 10 × (5/18)

⇒ 25/9

Let the length of the other train be x m

Now,

[(230 + x)/(25/9)] = 180

⇒ (230 + x) = 180 × (25/9)

⇒ 230 + x = 500

⇒ x = 270

So, length of the other train = 270 m

**∴ The length (in m) of the other train is 270.**

questions.question: If a² + b² = 65 and ab = 8, a > b > 0, then find the value of a² - b².
questions.solution:
**Given:**

a2 + b2 = 65 and ab = 8

**Concept used:**

(a + b)2 = a2 + b2 + 2a

(a - b)2 = a2 + b2 - 2ab

a2 - b2 = (a + b)(a - b)

**Calculation:**

a2 + b2 + 2ab = 65 + 16

⇒ (a + b)2 = 81

⇒ (a + b) = 9

Again,

a2 + b2 - 2ab = 65 - 16

⇒ (a - b)2 = 49

⇒ (a - b) = 7

Now,

a2 - b2 = 9 × 7

⇒ a2 - b2 = 63

**∴ Required answer is 63.

questions.question: AB and CD are two chords in a circle with centre O and AD is the diameter. When produced, AB and CD meet at the point P. If ∠DAP = 27°, ∠APD = 35°, then what is the measure (in degrees) of ∠DBC?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

∠DAP = 27°, ∠APD = 35°

**Concept used:**

The angle subtended by the diameter at any point on the circumference is equal to 90°

Angles subtended by an arc in the same segment of the circle are equal.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a398bd9bc2906e47e2a3a150a0f7cdb602ae4a7a0a4d579e3d26115fb020c9d7.png] 

In the given figure

∠DCA = ∠DBA = 90°

In ΔPCA

∠PAC = 180° - 90° - 35°

⇒ ∠PAC = 55°

Now,

∠DAC = 55° - 27°

⇒ ∠DAC = 28°

According to the concept,

∠DAC = ∠DBC = 28

**∴ The measure (in degrees) of ∠DBC is 28.**

questions.question: A tyre has two punctures. The first puncture alone would have made the tyre flat in 45 minutes, and the second puncture alone would have done it in 90 minutes. If air leaks out at a constant rate, then how long (in minutes) does it take for both the punctures together to make the tyre flat?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The first puncture alone would have made the tyre flat in 45 minutes

The second puncture alone would have done it in 90 minutes. 

**Concept used:**

Total work = Efficiency of an object × time taken by the object

**Calculation:**

LCM of 45 and 90 = 90 units i.e total work

So, efficiency of 1st puncture = 90/45 = 2 units/min

efficiency of 2nd puncture = 90/90 = 1 unit/min

Effective efficiency of both the puncture = 3 units/min

Time taken to flat the tyre by both the puncture = 90/3

⇒ 30 min

**∴ It takes 30 (in minutes) for both the punctures together to make the tyre flat.**

questions.question: A and B entered into a partnership with investments in the ratio 3 ∶ 5. After a few months, A withdrew and collected his money back. At the end of the year, they received profit in the ratio 2 ∶ 5. For how many months did A invest?
questions.solution:

A and B entered into a partnership with investments in the ratio 3 ∶ 5.

**Calculation:**

Let A invest for x months

questions.question: What is the sum of the numbers between 400 and 500 such that when they are divided by 6, 12 and 16, it leaves no remainder?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

We need to find the sum of numbers in the range of 400 - 500 such that they are divisible by each 6, 12 and 16.

**Calculation:**

LCM (6, 12, 16) = 48k

The required numbers will be in the form of 48k, where k is a natural number.

For k = 9,

48k = 48 × 9

⇒ 432

For k = 10,

48k = 48 × 10

⇒ 480

Now,

Only 432 and 480 is the number that are between 400 and 500, and also divisible by 6, 12 and 16

Sum = 432 + 480

⇒ 912

**∴ The required sum of the numbers is 912.**

questions.question:
A solid cone of radius 7 cm and height 7 cm was melted along with two solid spheres of radius 7 cm each to form a solid cylinder of radius 7 cm. What is the curved surface area (in cm²) of the cylinder?

(Use π = (22)/(7))
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A solid cone of radius 7 cm and height 7 cm was melted along with two solid spheres of radius 7 cm each to form a solid cylinder of radius 7 cm.

**Formula used:**

The volume of a cone = 1/3πr²h

Volume of a cylinder = πr2h

The volume of a sphere = 4/3πr3

The curved surface area of a cylinder = 2πrh

Here,

r = radius

h = height

**Calculation:**

The volume of the cone = 1/3π × 7² × 7

⇒ 1/3π × 73

The volume of each sphere = 4/3π × 73

Let the height of the formed cylinder be H

According to the question,

1/3π × 73 + 2 × 4/3π × 73 = π × 7² × H

⇒ 73π.(1/3 + 8/3) = π × 72 × H

⇒ 7 × (9/3) = H

⇒ 7 × 3 = H

⇒ 21 = H

So, the height of the formed cylinder is 21 cm

Now,

The curved surface area of the cylinder = 2 × 22/7 × 7 × 21

⇒ 924

**∴ The curved surface area (in cm2) of the cylinder is 924.**

questions.question: The selling price of a mobile phone is Rs. 59,620 and it was sold at 8.4% profit. The cost price (in Rs.) of the mobile phone is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The selling price of a mobile phone is Rs. 59,620 and it was sold at 8.4% profit. 

**Concept used:**

Selling price = Cost price + cost price × profit%

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price of the mobile phone be Rs. 100x

Now,

100x + 100x × 8.4% = 59620

⇒ 108.4x = 59620

⇒ x = 59620/108.4

⇒ x = 550

So, cost price = 100 × 550

⇒ Rs. 55000

**∴ The cost price (in Rs.) of the mobile phone is 55000.**

questions.question: If x⁴ - 79x² + 1 = 0, then a value of x + x⁻¹ can be:
